problem: Internal architecture of 'chain_router' (type: Service — A deployable runtime component that handles requests, performs work, or coordinates other components). Node: Per-chain routing service: receives authenticated RPC requests carrying an explicit (chain, fork) tag, selects a healthy non-draining replica from the matching fork sub-pool of the region's chain pool, enforces per-tenant query cost budgets, isolates heavy historical queries onto the historical-replica subset, observes replica-level chain-head and fork-allegiance signals and reports them to region_coordinator (which computes a quorum-based canonical tip per (chain, fork) across all regions); for high-value reads against tip, requires the canonical tip from region_coordinator rather than treating its region's pool as authoritative. Every head observation submitted to region_coordinator's tip_quorum is tagged with the authenticated source replica identity of the submitting chain_router replica, signed over the cert-bearing inter-region surface (mTLS to region_coordinator), so region_coordinator's tip_quorum can attribute each observation to a specific chain_router replica and apply per-source rate limiting and adversarial-source quarantine. Canonicalizes every JSON-RPC response leaving a chain pool against a per-(chain, method, schema_version) schema before forwarding to gateway: undocumented optional fields stripped or sorted, types coerced, intra-response ordering rules applied so response shape is independent of which client implementation answered. Quarantines replicas whose canonicalized response shape diverges from pool consensus the same way it quarantines tip-divergent replicas; partitions a chain pool by replica fork allegiance so cross-fork divergence is sub-pool membership, not quarantine. Detects unannounced consensus splits (replicas in a pool diverging into two stable subgroups, neither a transient reorg) and emits a 'fork-detected' alert with a documented operator-decision SLA before the split becomes user-visible. Measures each pool's tip lag against an out-of-band reference (peer-regional pools via region_coordinator, plus chain peer count / expected slot advance) and marks pools 'tip-stale' when they exceed a per-chain freshness budget; tip-stale pools are excluded from canonical-tip quorum and gateway annotates responses they answer. Exposes an explicit pool-drain protocol: a replica entering 'draining' state stops receiving new requests, finishes in-flight RPCs (or returns them with a retryable-on-other-replica hint), and only after gateway has re-bound any dependent subscriptions does the replica unsubscribe from fanout's head streams. Schema-skew and tip-divergence quarantines consult region_coordinator's 'rotation in progress' tag and suppress quarantines triggered solely by the documented rotation window. At RPC submission time it returns a per-method cost-class hint (short-RPC vs long-RPC, with expected wall-clock band and resource profile) so callers can partition their in-flight slot pool. Cancels in-flight long-RPCs for offboarded tenants, deduping cancellation signals by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meeting a documented attestation SLO and surfacing preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when an in-flight long-RPC overlaps a preservation hold) so region_coordinator can record best-effort attestations on timeout. Cert-bearing surface for mTLS to chain pool replicas and to region_coordinator's tip_quorum, enumerated in cert-inventory. Connections: gateway --calls-> chain_router; chain_router --proxies_to-> eth_archive; chain_router --proxies_to-> sepolia_archive; chain_router --proxies_to-> btc_archive; chain_router --proxies_to-> ada_archive; chain_router --calls-> region_coordinator. Parent requirements: R-response-canonicalization: Every JSON-RPC response forwarded from a chain pool through chain_router is canonicalized against a per-chain, per-method schema before it reaches gateway: undocumented optional fields are stripped or sorted, types are coerced, and intra-response ordering rules are applied so that response shape is a function of (chain, method, schema_version) and is independent of which client implementation in the pool produced it.; R-schema-skew-quarantine: When a chain pool replica produces responses whose canonicalized shape differs from the pool consensus shape for the same (method, schema_version), chain_router quarantines that replica from the active pool the same way it quarantines a divergent-tip replica, and surfaces the skew to operators.; R-pool-drain-protocol: chain_router exposes an explicit drain state for chain pool replicas: a draining replica receives no new requests, finishes in-flight RPCs (or returns a retryable-on-other-replica signal to gateway), and only unsubscribes from fanout's head streams after gateway has re-bound the affected subscriptions to a non-draining replica.; R-rotation-aware-skew: Schema-skew quarantine and tip-divergence quarantine both consult a 'rotation in progress' tag from region_coordinator and suppress quarantines triggered solely by the documented rotation window, so rotation noise does not look like a misbehaving replica.; R-tip-freshness-budget: Each chain has an explicit per-chain tip-freshness budget (max acceptable lag from upstream chain tip). chain_router measures pool tip lag against an out-of-band reference (peer-regional pools, chain peer count, expected slot advance) and marks the pool 'tip-stale' when it exceeds the budget.; R-fork-identity: Every chain has an explicit, documented set of supported forks identified by (chain_id, fork_id). chain_router partitions each chain pool by fork allegiance; replicas on different forks belong to different sub-pools and are not treated as divergent under R-chain-cross-check.; R-fork-detection-alert: Detection of an unannounced consensus split (replicas in a pool diverging into two stable subgroups, neither a transient reorg) surfaces a 'fork-detected' alert with a documented operator-decision SLA before the split is exposed to tenants as a separate fork sub-pool.

versions.note: v1: addressed Session 1 stressors (15 breaking, 1 survives, 27 derived reqs satisfied). response_canonicalizer gained explicit canonical-bytes-version spec + independent validator path distinct from transform path. schema_skew_quarantine gained per-(schema_version, canonical-bytes-version) cohort scoping, canonicalizer-fault vs replica-skew verdict distinction, per-(chain, fork_id) max-concurrent-quarantine cap, rotation-tag hlc-stamping with commit-time re-check, rotation event-type discrimination. tip_freshness_tracker gained HLC-degraded freeze with explicit no-wallclock-fallback, optional chain-derived signals tagged hlc-degraded, rotation event-type discrimination. fork_detection_alerter gained K-replica local stability gate + self-rate-limit within tip_quorum's per-source budget. sub_pool_fork_partitioner gained routing-table fork-transition hlc fence, cost-class-aware routing, effective-capacity denominator. pool_membership_manager gained drain_state_log CAS gating + explicit drain-abort, on-dispatch fork revalidation, safe-membership floor refusal, target-capacity rebalance, replica-class admission, M-of-N operator override, max-overrides-per-window. drain_coordinator gained bounded drain-completion wait with operator-override force-complete, authenticated rebind-ack with per-drain nonce, force-completed and drain-stuck transitions. pool_registry sharded per (chain, fork_id) with independent CAS lines; replica-class, canonical-bytes-version, freshness-derivation tag added. drain_state_log carries authenticated ack signature and per-drain nonce. One req bubbled to parent: lifecycle_gate operator-credential model (M-of-N, rotation, compromise-revocation, audit) for chain_router pool-admit override — same parent concern as tip_quorum's bubble.

v2 — Direction 18 chain_router Session 2 against v1. 14 stressors all BREAKING, 15 derived reqs all satisfied + 8 inherited v9-era reqs all satisfied + 2 bubbles to parent (named-roster fetch endpoint, fanout fork-transition handshake-ack contract). drain_coordinator gained: lifecycle_gate-scheduled drain windows (HLC TTL-bounded per-replica leases; drain-window-expired typed terminal state; lease-holder crash leaves drain-stuck-after-crash for next-window continuation; never autonomously force-completes under expired window); drain-fence broadcast consumer with named-roster verification (on-demand named-roster fetch from region_coordinator, HLC-bounded budget, bulk-wave coalescing, named-roster-unfetchable / named-roster-fetch-failed-bulk attestations); durable phase-markers (RECEIVED/FLUSH-IN-PROGRESS/FLUSH-COMPLETE/ACK-EMITTED/ATTESTATION-WRITTEN/TERMINAL-ACK/TERMINAL-PRESERVATION-BLOCKED) per (offboarding_id, component_id, drain_id); drain-ack-handoff record for teardown-overlap; drain-fence-vs-fork-transition fence; canonical writer election (CAS) for terminal-class attestation. pool_membership_manager gained: drain-fence broadcast consumer (mirror of drain_coordinator); priority-lane CAS for drain-fence pre-empting deferred-quarantine; named-roster verification at override-commit time with retroactive-as-of-HLC compromise-revocation evaluation and atomic re-check with pool_registry CAS; cost-class-hint-required dispatch refusal. sub_pool_fork_partitioner gained: cost-class hint preservation on retryable-on-other-replica responses; structured fork-transition handshake to fanout (chain_id, prior fork_id, new fork_id, divergence HLC, prior fork terminal HLC); fanout-handshake-ack fence on per-(chain, fork_id) shard before forward-progress admit; fork-transition-pending degraded mode when fanout-suspended. fork_detection_alerter gained: deferred-quarantine cohort filter for tip_quorum submission; fork-transition handshake driver; named-roster verification on signed broadcasts. schema_skew_quarantine gained: canonicalizer-fault verdict structurally orthogonal to rotation-tag suppression (always recorded, published to compliance_audit). tip_freshness_tracker gained: deferred-quarantine cohort filter on freshness aggregate; fork-transition-pending freshness suspension. pool_registry gained: fanout-handshake-ack state per shard (pending/acked/suspended); drain-fence-priority CAS line tag. drain_state_log gained: drain-window-expired, drain-stuck-after-crash, drain-ack-handoff record types; per-(offboarding_id, component_id, drain_id) phase-markers; lifecycle_gate window_id and HLC TTL evidence per entry. Two bubbles to parent: bubble-chain_router-2 (named-roster fetch endpoint on region_coordinator's credential_roster), bubble-chain_router-3 (fanout fork-transition handshake-ack contract — deferred to fanout zoom). NKP K̄=1.50, P̄=0.79, modularity=0.13, CRITICAL regime preserved; single hotspot pool_registry K=7 unchanged from v1.

stressors.description: A new replica software version emits a JSON-RPC response that is technically valid against the schema but uses a previously-unseen optional field ordering or numeric type widening not yet covered by canonicalization rules. The canonicalizer's transform path produces a stable canonical form, but its emitted bytes drift from older replicas' canonical bytes for the same logical response — subscribers caching by canonical-byte hash see two answers for the same query.
stressors.attractor: Canonicalizer's schema repository defines what to strip/coerce/sort but not the bytes-of-canonical-output. Without a documented byte-level canonical spec, canonical bytes are an emergent property of the canonicalizer's implementation — a code change to the canonicalizer (or a new field unseen in the repository) silently changes canonical-byte identity for unchanged logical content.
stressors.solution: Canonicalizer rejects (chain, method, schema_version) tuples lacking a registered canonical-bytes-version; canonical-bytes-version is bumped when ordering or type-representation policy changes; subscribers comparing canonical-byte hashes can scope hash equivalence to a canonical-bytes-version.

stressors.description: During a fork transition (a new fork_id becomes documented), some chain pool replicas have already moved to the new fork while others still serve the old. The partitioner's routing table is rebuilt from pool_registry, but a stream of in-flight requests carrying the old fork tag arrives during the rebuild. A subset of these requests reads a stale routing table snapshot and is routed to a replica that has just moved to the new fork — answering with new-fork data under an old-fork request label.
stressors.attractor: Routing table rebuild on every membership transition is non-atomic from the requesting thread's perspective; the partitioner's read of the routing table and the replica's read of its own current fork_id are decoupled, so a request can pass routing under fork-A's table and arrive at a replica that just transitioned to fork-B.
stressors.solution: Two-fence approach: routing-table rebuild stamps the fork-transition hlc_stamp and refuses dispatch under stale stamps; on dispatch, pool_membership_manager re-checks the replica's current fork_id against the request's fork tag and returns retryable-on-other-replica on mismatch.

stressors.description: drain_coordinator has driven a replica through draining and is about to commit eviction. Concurrently, an operator (or pool_membership_manager via auto-admit) decides to re-admit the same replica because health checks recovered. The membership manager writes admit, the drain commits eviction; depending on the order of writes to pool_registry the replica ends up in evicted state with a routing-table entry that points to it, or the eviction overwrites a fresh admit, leaving the recovered replica unservable.
stressors.attractor: pool_registry transitions are not gated on drain_state_log: drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager both have write authority on pool_registry without a single CAS line ordering their proposals.
stressors.solution: Pool_registry transitions gated by drain_state_log via CAS; re-admit during drain requires explicit drain-abort with attribution before admit commits.

stressors.description: A legitimate schema-version rollout overlaps a region_coordinator rotation-in-progress window: as replicas pick up the new schema_version, they emit canonicalized shapes that diverge from the (old) pool consensus. Each new-schema replica is tagged with rotation-in-progress at observation, so its quarantine is suppressed. But once the rotation tag clears at its documented timeout while the rollout is still partial, the deferred quarantines all commit at once — evicting all newly-rolled-out replicas in a cascade and leaving the sub-pool with only old-schema replicas.
stressors.attractor: Rotation-suppression converts rotation-window quarantines into deferred quarantines but does not distinguish 'divergence due to rolling new schema_version' from 'divergence due to misbehaving replica'. A schema_version rollout looks identical to a quarantine candidate plus rotation tag; once the tag's suppression timeout fires, the deferred quarantines stampede.
stressors.solution: Three-fence: schema_version-aware divergence (canonical-bytes-version cohort), per-sub-pool quarantine commit-rate cap, and a sub-pool membership floor enforced at pool_membership_manager that refuses quarantine evictions that would breach it.

stressors.description: region_coordinator's HLC enters degraded mode (per region_coordinator's spec, the degraded mode is signalled). tip_freshness_tracker continues measuring tip lag, but its lag computation falls back to local wall-clock for the freshness budget comparison because the HLC stamp is unreliable. Wall-clock skew between this region and the peer-regional reference makes pools look fresh-or-stale depending on which side of the skew they sit on; the per-pool tip-stale flag becomes a function of clock skew, and tip_quorum at region_coordinator gets misleading exclusions.
stressors.attractor: The freshness measurement requires SOME timestamp comparison; HLC-degraded means region_coordinator's freshness signal is unreliable for the lifetime of degraded mode. Falling back to local wall-clock generates lies; freezing the tracker entirely means stale flags become permanently stuck.
stressors.solution: On HLC-degraded, tip_freshness_tracker freezes the tip-stale set and refuses wall-clock fallback. Optional chain-derived signals can be used but are tagged hlc-degraded so tip_quorum applies them conservatively.

stressors.description: fork_detection_alerter submits every observed (chain, fork_id) candidate to region_coordinator's tip_quorum, including transient candidates that haven't yet stabilized into a real fork (single-replica observations, brief reorgs). At pool scale, the per-region per-source rate limit at tip_quorum is hit by fork_detection_alerter alone, drowning out legitimate observations from other chain_router replicas. The submission flood is from chain_router's own side and looks identical to a malicious replica from tip_quorum's perspective.
stressors.attractor: fork_detection_alerter has no submission policy beyond 'send observations to tip_quorum'; it submits raw observations without local pre-filtering for stability, so transient candidates and stable-fork candidates compete on the same rate budget.
stressors.solution: fork_detection_alerter pre-filters submissions on local stability (K-replica confirmation in window) and self-rate-limits within tip_quorum's documented per-source budget so its submissions don't crowd out legitimate ones.

stressors.description: A single (chain, fork_id) sub-pool absorbs the bulk of regional traffic (e.g. mainnet ETH dominant fork). Replica capacity within chain_router's pool budget is allocated by sub-pool membership, not by traffic share. The dominant sub-pool's replicas saturate; rare-fork sub-pools have proportionally over-allocated headroom but cannot serve dominant-fork traffic. Latency tail for dominant-fork users spikes while idle replicas in rare-fork sub-pools cannot shed load.
stressors.attractor: Sub-pool partitioning is a strict membership boundary: a replica belongs to exactly one (chain, fork_id) sub-pool. There is no admission-class beyond 'in this sub-pool', so capacity cannot be re-balanced under load.
stressors.solution: Capacity rebalance is an explicit, audited operation through pool_membership_manager — not a runtime spillover that would violate fork-membership semantics.

stressors.description: Several replicas in a sub-pool are simultaneously in deferred-quarantine (rotation-tag suppression) or in draining state for a maintenance window. The remaining healthy set is a small fraction of nominal capacity. pool_membership_manager continues admitting requests at the nominal rate because routing-table size includes deferred-quarantine and draining replicas (they're not yet evicted). Latency tails grow because requests queue at fewer-than-expected serving replicas.
stressors.attractor: Routing fan-out budgets are derived from pool_registry membership counts, but the relevant denominator for per-replica load is healthy-non-draining-non-deferred-quarantine count. The two diverge during a partial-quarantine or partial-drain window.
stressors.solution: Effective-capacity denominator computed from pool_registry's lifecycle flags (admitted AND not draining AND not deferred-quarantine AND not tip-stale); routing and admission use the effective denominator, not raw membership.

stressors.description: response_canonicalizer's transform path and schema_skew_quarantine's divergence-detection path both consume the same schema/canonical-bytes-version repository. A bug or a malformed schema entry produces a transform that subtly mis-orders a field AND a divergence-detector that flags everything else as deviating from this mis-ordered consensus. The same source bug both serves wrong canonical bytes to consumers and quarantines the entire pool. They are sub-roles in name only — they share a fate.
stressors.attractor: The naive design has the canonicalizer 'expose the canonical-shape signal to schema_skew_quarantine via a documented internal interface' — i.e. the same schema repository, possibly the same in-process loaded state, drives both. The split is illusory; a single bug splits both.
stressors.solution: Independent canonical-bytes validator path with separate code/state from the transform; schema_skew_quarantine consumes validator verdicts and distinguishes canonicalizer-fault from replica-skew verdicts so a canonicalizer bug doesn't quarantine the pool.

stressors.description: An emergency rollover of pool replicas (e.g. zero-day in chain client) needs to admit replacement replicas faster than the documented blue/green wave allows. An operator can issue a pool-admit override at chain_router that bypasses the safe-membership-floor refusal. A single compromised operator credential can mass-admit attacker-controlled replicas into an active sub-pool. The override path lives at chain_router, but the credential model that authorizes it lives at parent (region_coordinator's lifecycle_gate).
stressors.attractor: chain_router's pool-admit override path needs a parent-scope authorization model. Implementing M-of-N quorum signing locally in pool_membership_manager would duplicate the same credential model tip_quorum bubbled. The credential model is parent's responsibility.
stressors.solution: Local M-of-N gating in pool_membership_manager plus a max-overrides-per-window rate limit; the parent-scope credential authorization model (key custody, rotation, compromise-revocation, per-operator audit) is bubbled to root scope.

stressors.description: schema_skew_quarantine and tip_freshness_tracker each cache the rotation-in-progress tag from region_coordinator on a polling cadence. If the tag clears at region_coordinator after a quarantine candidate is observed but before the cache refreshes, the suppression timer fires against the stale 'rotation-in-progress=true' read and a quarantine that should commit immediately is held for the rest of the cache window. Conversely, if the tag arrives late, a legitimate rotation-window divergence quarantines a clean replica before suppression kicks in.
stressors.attractor: Rotation-tag is read on a polling cadence; the read is local and stale by up-to-cache-interval. The decision to suppress is taken against the cached value, not against a live read at decision time.
stressors.solution: Each quarantine/transition proposal stamps the rotation-tag hlc_stamp at observation; suppression decisions are tied to that stamp; commit-time re-check forces re-evaluation if the tag changed in a way that invalidates the prior suppression.

stressors.description: drain_coordinator commits drain-completed only after gateway-rebind acknowledgement. If gateway is unable to ack within bounded time (slow-consumer subscriptions, fanout slowdown), drain stalls indefinitely, holding chain pool replicas in draining state and starving sub-pool capacity. Conversely, an unauthenticated or replayed rebind-ack from a compromised gateway path could prematurely complete the drain.
stressors.attractor: Drain-completion is gated on a single signal (gateway-rebind ack) without bound on wait time and without authenticated freshness. The ack signal is binary; there is no escalation path for stuck drains and no anti-replay protection.
stressors.solution: Bounded drain-completion wait with stuck-drain escalation (operator-override force-complete via M-of-N); rebind-ack carries authenticated signature plus per-drain nonce so replay or forgery cannot complete a drain.

stressors.description: All seven subservices read/write pool_registry. During a sub-pool-wide event (e.g. mass tip-stale flag set when peer-regional reference comes back online with a different head), tip_freshness_tracker writes a flurry of per-replica transitions; pool_membership_manager and sub_pool_fork_partitioner both read at high rate; schema_skew_quarantine reads pool_registry to compute consensus shape. K=7 hotspot from naive design — the registry becomes a contention point.
stressors.attractor: K=7 is 'all subservices touch pool_registry'. Without explicit per-(chain, fork_id) sharding the registry is one logical line; without read/write separation reads can starve writes.
stressors.solution: pool_registry sharded per (chain, fork_id) with independent CAS lines and shard-level summaries for cross-shard consumers — collapses the K=7 contention to per-shard contention bounded by sub-pool size.

stressors.description: chain_router's parent contract isolates heavy historical queries onto the historical-replica subset, separate from tip-serving replicas. The naive internal design has not modeled this — pool_registry has no replica-class flag; pool_membership_manager admits requests without distinguishing tip-RPC from archive-RPC. A burst of archive queries (eth_getLogs over wide block ranges) can saturate replicas that are also serving tip-sensitive RPCs.
stressors.attractor: The internal design omitted the replica-class dimension. Adding it requires another column in pool_registry and a routing rule based on cost-class hint.
stressors.solution: Add replica-class to pool_registry and route by cost-class so archive vs tip workloads partition replica capacity per the parent contract.

stressors.description: region_coordinator's 'rotation in progress' tag is set during cert rotation, origin-endpoint rotation, and chain-pool blue/green rotation. schema_skew_quarantine and tip_freshness_tracker treat the tag as a single suppression signal: any rotation suppresses both schema-skew quarantines and tip-divergence quarantines. But cert rotation has nothing to do with response shape; suppressing schema-skew during a cert rotation just creates an unmonitored window for skew.
stressors.attractor: The tag is overloaded — it conflates orthogonal events. Each event class has a different relationship to schema-skew vs tip-divergence quarantine.
stressors.solution: Consume rotation tag with explicit event-type discrimination: schema-skew suppresses only on chain-pool/chain-client-version rotations; tip-divergence suppresses only on chain-pool rotations; cert/origin rotations don't suppress quarantine paths.

stressors.description: An offboarded tenant's in-flight long-RPC sits on a draining replica and overlaps a preservation hold. The naive design's IR-offboarding-idempotency calls for surfacing preservation-blocked terminal state. drain_coordinator hits this case: the long-RPC cannot be cancelled (preservation hold), but the replica is draining and waiting to evict. Should the drain wait, or should the long-RPC be migrated to another replica? Both subservices have correct local rules but their interaction at this corner needs to be definite.
stressors.attractor: drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager each have a rule (drain waits for completion, preservation-blocked surfaces best-effort attestation), and the rules compose: drain waits, the long-RPC continues on the draining replica until preservation hold resolves or the long-RPC times out, then drain completes. The drain-completion wait bound (SR-drain-rebind-ack-bounded) caps the wait.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate reserves a drain window for chain_router; drain_coordinator starts the drain and acquires the per-replica mutex/lease, but the lifecycle_gate window's HLC TTL expires while a long-RPC is still draining (gateway-rebind ack pending). What happens — does drain_coordinator continue under an expired window (violating the single-scheduler-of-record contract), abort with the replica stuck in draining, or attempt force-complete?
stressors.attractor: drain_coordinator continues under expired window (silent contract violation), or aborts leaving replica in indefinite draining state, or invokes force-complete with no clean attribution to the window expiry vs gateway-rebind-stall.
stressors.solution: drain_coordinator stamps every drain start with the lifecycle_gate window's HLC TTL; if the window expires while the drain is in flight, the drain transitions to drain-window-expired in drain_state_log (a new typed terminal state distinct from drain-stuck and force-completed), refuses further per-replica work under the expired window, surfaces an alert with attribution naming the lifecycle_gate window_id, and the replica remains in 'draining' until a NEW lifecycle_gate-reserved window admits a continuation drain (no autonomous force-complete under expired window). Re-entry under the new window resumes from drain_state_log's last durable phase rather than restarting.

stressors.description: A drain-fence broadcast for tenant T arrives while schema_skew_quarantine is mid-cascade (multiple replicas being deferred-quarantined under the per-(chain,fork) max-concurrent cap). pool_membership_manager must flush in-flight audit writes for T to compliance_audit and ack within the HLC ack window, but pool_registry's per-(chain,fork) shard CAS line is contended by the quarantine commits. Does the ack window expire? Is there a deadlock between quarantine deferral commits and drain-fence flush?
stressors.attractor: Drain-ack window expires while pool_registry shard CAS is contended; pool_membership_manager either misses the ack (causing tenant_store erasure to finalize as STRICT-incomplete) or commits the ack while quarantine commits race past the safe-membership floor. No priority discipline between drain-fence flush and quarantine cascade.
stressors.solution: Drain-fence flush is admitted on a separate priority lane than quarantine commits on the per-(chain,fork) pool_registry shard CAS line: drain-fence transitions are tagged drain-fence-priority and pre-empt deferred-quarantine commits within the shard; deferred-quarantines wait until drain-fence ack-emitted; pool_membership_manager surfaces an alert when quarantine deferral grows under drain-fence pressure. compliance_audit writes for drain-fence flush are batched per tenant and emitted before ack.

stressors.description: An offboarding signal (or drain-fence broadcast) arrives signed under roster_version V_named that chain_router has never seen — V_named is strictly newer than the local cache and has not yet been ack-readied. Per the parent contract, broadcasts are self-contained credential bundles to be verified against the named roster_version. Can chain_router verify? If not, can it silently fall back to local cache (violating the contract)? If it rejects, the offboarding stalls and the attestation SLO is violated.
stressors.attractor: chain_router silently falls back to local cache (contract violation) and admits the broadcast without verification, OR rejects the broadcast and the offboarding signal is dropped causing tenant_store to time out the per-tenant ack window into STRICT-erasure-incomplete. No on-demand named-roster fetch path.
stressors.solution: chain_router exposes an on-demand named-roster fetch path: when a broadcast names V_named that is strictly newer than the local cache, chain_router synchronously requests V_named from region_coordinator (over the cert-bearing inter-region surface) before verifying the broadcast; the fetch is bounded by a documented HLC budget tighter than the per-tenant ack window; on fetch failure within budget, chain_router rejects the broadcast and emits a typed 'named-roster-unfetchable' attestation to compliance_audit with the broadcast's offboarding_id, allowing tenant_store/lifecycle_gate to decide STRICT vs PARTIAL-WITH-WITNESSES finalization with full attribution.

stressors.description: fork_detection_alerter declares (eth, fork_A→fork_B) repartition; sub_pool_fork_partitioner installs new routing table at HLC fence; pool_membership_manager commits new sub-pool membership. But fork-transition handshake to fanout requires fanout to ack rollback-to-divergence-point before chain_router dispatches forward-progress on fork_B. What if fanout has already started serving forward-progress events on fork_A's tip stream from chain_router's earlier observations and a per-cursor monotonicity guarantee prevents replaying back to the divergence point? Or fanout takes longer than chain_router's drain TTL to ack?
stressors.attractor: chain_router dispatches forward-progress on new fork before fanout acks handshake (causing fanout to ship forward-progress events before the rollback notification — violating the parent's r-s4-fork-transition-rollback-contract), or stalls indefinitely on fanout's ack.
stressors.solution: sub_pool_fork_partitioner admits forward-progress dispatch on the new fork only AFTER a fanout-handshake-ack is recorded in pool_registry's per-(chain, fork_id) shard with the divergence-point's HLC; until then, requests tagged with the new fork_id are bounced (retryable-on-other-region-or-later-time) rather than served. The handshake includes the divergence-point and the prior fork's terminal HLC observed by chain_router, giving fanout deterministic input for its rollback notification. Handshake timeout exceeding a documented bound surfaces fork-transition-stalled alert and chain_router does not unilaterally unblock dispatch.

stressors.description: drain_coordinator holds the per-(chain,fork,replica) drain mutex/lease bounded by the lifecycle_gate window's HLC TTL. The drain_coordinator instance crashes mid-drain (after RECEIVED phase, before ACK-EMITTED). On restart, the replica re-attempts. Without phase-markers persisted durably, can the new instance re-run flush from scratch (potential double-write to compliance_audit)? Can a stale lease be released cleanly? Does pool_membership_manager see the replica stuck in 'draining' indefinitely?
stressors.attractor: Replica stuck in 'draining' indefinitely until manual operator intervention; double-flush to compliance_audit on restart; orphan lease blocks future drain windows from being scheduled by lifecycle_gate.
stressors.solution: drain_coordinator persists durable per-(offboarding_id, component_id, drain_id) phase-markers in drain_state_log (RECEIVED, FLUSH-IN-PROGRESS, FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, TERMINAL); on restart the new instance reads the latest marker for the lease and resumes from there (never re-runs flush if FLUSH-COMPLETE is durable). Per-(chain, fork_id, replica) drain leases are bounded by the lifecycle_gate window's HLC TTL: lease-holder crash without TERMINAL within the window leaves the replica in a documented 'drain-stuck-after-crash' state visible to lifecycle_gate, allowing the next lifecycle_gate window to admit a continuation lease.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate has scheduled BOTH a chain-pool blue/green rotation (rotation-tag=chain-pool-blue-green) AND a drain window for replicas of the rotation's old colour. schema_skew_quarantine suppresses quarantine during rotation; drain_coordinator drains old replicas. But during the drain, a replica produces canonicalizer-fault-flagged output (validator rejection) — distinct from replica-skew. Should it suppress under rotation? Or is canonicalizer-fault structurally orthogonal to rotation-tag? Currently the rotation-tag lookup is at observation time. Does drain hide a real canonicalizer-fault?
stressors.attractor: canonicalizer-fault is suppressed under rotation tag (false-suppress); a real bug in the canonicalizer hides behind rotation noise during the drain; drained replicas leave service with no record of canonicalizer-fault for post-mortem.
stressors.solution: schema_skew_quarantine's canonicalizer-fault verdict is structurally orthogonal to the rotation-tag suppression: rotation suppression applies ONLY to replica-skew verdicts, never to canonicalizer-fault verdicts (which indicate a transform-path bug rather than a replica-shape divergence). canonicalizer-fault is always recorded and surfaced as its own alert, and the impacted replica is held in deferred-quarantine for canonicalizer-fault even during rotation+drain windows; the verdict is published to compliance_audit so post-mortem of the drained replica retains the evidence.

stressors.description: tip_freshness_tracker measures pool tip lag using the surviving replicas. A replica is mid-quarantine (deferred-quarantine, not yet committed) due to schema-skew but still serving tip observations. Its tip observations are still aggregated. If the replica is actually serving slightly stale tip — but is excluded from canonical-tip quorum at region_coordinator only after its tip-stale flag commits — there's a window where tip_freshness_tracker treats it as fresh while quarantine is deferred. Does this allow tip-stale signals into fork_detection_alerter submissions?
stressors.attractor: fork_detection_alerter submits head observations from a deferred-quarantine replica still treated as 'fresh' by tip_freshness_tracker; tip_quorum receives adversarial-source-tagged observations and may apply per-source rate limit / quarantine but the freshness flag is wrong.
stressors.solution: fork_detection_alerter's submission to tip_quorum filters its set of contributing replicas by pool_registry's deferred-quarantine flag (in addition to admitted/non-draining/non-tip-stale): a replica with deferred-quarantine for any reason is excluded from the freshness aggregate AND from the head-observation submission cohort; tip_freshness_tracker reads pool_registry's deferred-quarantine flag at observation time so the per-(chain, fork) freshness aggregate is computed only over replicas that would survive an immediate quarantine commit.

stressors.description: An offboarding signal arrives mid-flight for tenant T whose long-RPC is currently overlapping a preservation hold. drain_coordinator surfaces preservation-blocked terminal state. Meanwhile pool_membership_manager's drain-fence flow expects ACK-EMITTED before TERMINAL. Phase-markers don't currently distinguish 'preservation-blocked terminal' from 'ack-emitted terminal'. Can compliance_audit attestation be written for both? Can lifecycle_gate's ack-window expire while preservation hold is in force?
stressors.attractor: compliance_audit attestation written twice (once for preservation-blocked, once for ack-emit) or never (when ack-window expires while preservation hold is in force); phase-marker drift between drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager.
stressors.solution: Phase-marker taxonomy distinguishes TERMINAL-ACK (normal completion path: ACK-EMITTED then TERMINAL) from TERMINAL-PRESERVATION-BLOCKED (preservation hold prevented cancel; ack-window may have expired). Each terminal state writes exactly one typed attestation to compliance_audit with the (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) idempotency key and the terminal-class. drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager share the same drain_state_log entry; the attestation writer (whichever subsystem reaches TERMINAL first under the idempotency key) is the canonical writer.

stressors.description: RPC dispatch returns a per-method cost-class hint. A request initially routes to replica_X, gets a retryable-on-other-replica response (drain or fork mismatch). The retry comes back through sub_pool_fork_partitioner. Is the cost-class hint preserved on retry? If a long-RPC retry is mis-routed to a tip-only replica because the cost-class hint was lost in retry plumbing, the retry could starve the tip-serving subset.
stressors.attractor: Long-RPC retry routed to tip-only replica; tip-serving capacity saturated; SR-replica-class-tip-vs-archive's promise that 'pool_membership_manager refuses' is bypassed only when the cost-class hint is propagated; if hint is dropped on retry, refusal cannot trigger.
stressors.solution: sub_pool_fork_partitioner attaches the original cost-class hint to the retryable-on-other-replica response signal so the retry path (whether through gateway or internal pool_membership_manager re-dispatch) preserves it; pool_membership_manager refuses any dispatch lacking a cost-class hint when the request type requires one (long-RPC archive paths) and surfaces an alert if a cost-class-less retry arrives at dispatch.

stressors.description: pool_membership_manager has accepted a safe-membership-floor override proposal under M-of-N signatures from roster_version V. Before the proposal commits in pool_registry, region_coordinator publishes a compromise-revocation against one of the signing credentials with retroactive-as-of-HLC predating the proposal's submission. Does the proposal still commit? If commit happens before the revocation is acknowledged in chain_router's local cache, off-roster replica is admitted. If verification is against named roster_version (not local cache), how does retroactive revocation flow?
stressors.attractor: Off-roster replica admitted by pool_membership_manager because retroactive revocation arrives after commit; chain_router's commit-time roster_version check (against local cache) doesn't see the retroactive-as-of-HLC effect; subsequent quarantines or drains are operating on a tainted membership baseline.
stressors.solution: pool_membership_manager's override-commit path verifies the proposal against region_coordinator's currently-active roster_version (named-roster lookup, not local cache) at commit time, including evaluation of any retroactive-as-of-HLC compromise-revocation that predates the proposal's submission HLC; commit fails closed if any signing credential is retroactively revoked. Pre-commit roster_version is also re-checked atomically with the pool_registry CAS commit so the activation race cannot slip between roster check and registry commit.

stressors.description: A drain-fence broadcast for tenant T arrives while a fork-transition handshake to fanout is in progress (sub_pool_fork_partitioner has committed new routing table, but hasn't received fanout's ack). pool_membership_manager must flush in-flight audit writes for T to compliance_audit, but those writes may target replicas that are no longer in the active sub-pool post-handshake. Does the drain-ack reflect the pre- or post-transition state? Does flush-then-ack-then-teardown semantics survive a fork transition mid-fence?
stressors.attractor: drain-ack written against a stale routing-table view; flush misses tenant T's audit writes that landed on the post-transition sub-pool but were initiated against the pre-transition view; tenant_store certificate-of-deletion finalizes with incomplete coverage.
stressors.solution: Drain-fence flush is fenced against fork-transition handshake state: pool_membership_manager refuses to commit a drain-ack while a fork-transition handshake is mid-flight on any (chain, fork_id) shard whose audit writes for tenant T are in flight; the drain-fence ack window's HLC budget extends across the handshake completion or the broadcast is rejected with a typed 'drain-fence-blocked-by-fork-transition' attestation written to compliance_audit. Flush enumerates audit writes by tenant_id across both pre- and post-transition sub-pool views.

stressors.description: A chain_router replica is itself in lifecycle teardown when a drain-fence broadcast arrives for tenant T (the replica has 30s to terminate but flush would take 60s). Per the parent's r-s5-drain-fence-teardown-overlap, the replica must either flush-then-ack-then-teardown OR write a durable drain-ack-handoff record naming a successor. There is no current durable handoff mechanism in chain_router's spec. What happens — silent drop? unbounded teardown wait? lifecycle_gate stalls?
stressors.attractor: Silent drop of in-flight tenant T audit writes (lost-erasure evidence) or unbounded teardown wait that blocks lifecycle_gate's overall teardown sequencing for the region; no successor handoff mechanism.
stressors.solution: drain_state_log carries a typed drain-ack-handoff record (writes_to drain_state_log) naming a successor chain_router instance OR a persistent buffer (a tenant-T-flush-residual queue) that owns the residual flush; ack-by-handoff to tenant_store cites this record. lifecycle_gate's teardown-overlap rule (parent contract) forbids teardown completion while any drain-fence on this instance is unacked AND no drain-ack-handoff is recorded; drain_coordinator refuses teardown unless one of the two is true. Idempotent successor read of drain_state_log resumes the flush.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate emits a wave of bulk-offboarding broadcasts (per r-s5-drain-fence-bounded-batching). Each broadcast names roster_version V_new. chain_router's local roster cache is at V_old (V_old < V_new). Per IIR-broadcast-named-roster-verify, chain_router verifies against the named V_new — but if V_new is unknown locally, all bulk broadcasts are rejected, missing the per-tenant ack window in cascade. Is there a fast-path to fetch the named V_new on demand from region_coordinator? Or does the entire wave fail?
stressors.attractor: Cascade of rejected broadcasts; per-tenant ack windows expire across the wave; tenant_store finalizes many erasures as STRICT-incomplete; manual remediation backlog.
stressors.solution: Bulk-offboarding wave triggers a single named-roster fetch for the shared roster_version (not per-broadcast): pool_membership_manager and drain_coordinator coalesce on the named-roster lookup so the wave does not trigger N fetch operations; on fetch success the wave proceeds; on fetch failure, all broadcasts in the wave are rejected with a single typed 'named-roster-fetch-failed-bulk' attestation including the wave-id, allowing lifecycle_gate to retry the wave with bounded backoff before STRICT finalization.

stressors.description: fork_detection_alerter triggers fork-transition handshake to fanout. fanout is in fanout-suspended state in this region (per the gateway_health_surface). chain_router cannot dispatch forward-progress events on the new fork until fanout acks the handshake. Does the new fork's tip-traffic stall indefinitely in this region? Should chain_router degrade — refuse fork-tagged requests for the new fork until fanout returns? Or proceed with a documented unsafe forward-dispatch?
stressors.attractor: Tip-traffic on new fork stalls (effectively unavailable in region); or chain_router unsafely dispatches forward-progress without ack, violating rollback-before-forward-progress contract; or chain_router has no documented degraded mode for this case.
stressors.solution: When fanout's handshake-ack is unavailable (fanout-suspended in region per gateway_health_surface), chain_router enters a documented fork-transition-pending degraded mode for the affected (chain, fork_id): refuses dispatch tagged with the new fork_id with a typed 'fork-transition-pending' error so callers can retry against another region or wait; tip_freshness_tracker treats the new sub-pool's tip-freshness as suspended; chain_router NEVER dispatches forward-progress on the new fork without a fanout ack. The degraded state surfaces an alert and is observable on the gateway_health_surface so edge-side residency-aware routing can shift traffic.
